## Toronto Rent Increase Response Plan

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

A 7% increase on **CAD 2,400** would make the new monthly rent **CAD 2,568**. Since your lease is month-to-month, the safest move is to verify the notice, timing, and any rent-control details before you reply.

## What to Check Before You Respond

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clipboard-check.svg

| Step | What to do | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm the increase is in writing | You want the exact effective date, amount, and any form used |
| 2 | Calculate the new rent | 2,400 × 1.07 = **2,568** |
| 3 | Check the notice period | Month-to-month changes usually still require proper advance notice |
| 4 | Verify rent-control status | Rules can differ depending on when the unit was first occupied |
| 5 | Gather your lease and payment history | Helps if you need to compare the proposed increase to prior terms |
| 6 | Save all messages | Keep email, letter, screenshots, and dates in one place |
| 7 | Reply without agreeing yet | Acknowledge receipt and ask for clarification first |

### New Rent Calculation
- Current rent: **CAD 2,400**
- Increase rate: **7%**
- Increase amount: **CAD 168**
- Proposed new rent: **CAD 2,568/month**

### Documents to Gather
- Current lease or any renewal/extension documents
- The landlord’s written rent increase notice
- Rent payment records for the last 12 months
- Any prior notices or amendments
- Photos or notes showing the unit address and tenancy start date
- Any emails/texts about repairs, rent, or occupancy dates
- A copy of your own timeline: when you moved in, when rent changed before, and when notices were received

### Practical Response Checklist
- Confirm whether the notice gives enough lead time before **2026-01-01**
- Check whether the increase is tied to the correct rent amount and unit
- Compare the request with your lease terms and prior notices
- Ask whether the landlord is using the standard notice form
- If anything looks unclear, respond in writing and do not pay the new amount until you understand the request
- Keep paying the current rent on time while you clarify, unless you decide otherwise after reviewing the notice

## Polite Email Draft to Ask for Clarification

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/envelope.svg

Subject: Request for Rent Increase Details

Hello [Landlord’s Name],

Thank you for your message regarding the proposed rent increase starting on 2026-01-01.

I’d like to confirm a few details before I respond:
- The exact new monthly rent amount
- The notice period being provided
- The form or written notice being used
- Whether this increase follows the applicable rules for my tenancy

For reference, my current rent is CAD 2,400 per month, and a 7% increase would bring it to CAD 2,568 per month. Please let me know if that is the amount you intend to request.

Once I have the written details, I’ll review everything carefully and get back to you.

Thank you,
[Your Name]
[Apartment Address]
